decision: Harden executable lifecycle transactions as an unreleased post-v2.1.1 patch
rationale: Public-only adversarial tests confirmed partial-state commits, a same-pair interleaving gap, orphan checkpoints, late close validation, receipt binding and path-safety gaps, and rollback that could lose peer changes; a local per-repository transaction guard, complete-before-visible artifacts, focused compensation, and ownership validation repair those defects without adding distributed locking or claiming they are in the immutable v2.1.1 artifact.

decision: Sanitize live project state from packaged templates
rationale: The offline tarball smoke confirmed that build-time template mirroring could copy source-repository sessions, decisions, and checkpoints into fresh consumer projects; packaging now preserves scaffold structure while resetting live state, and smoke coverage enforces the boundary.

decision: Determine pristine handoffs from parsed canonical identity fields
rationale: Whole-document anchored regexes can match placeholder examples inside fenced Open Threads content; parser-derived values identify the actual canonical fields, while containing parse exceptions preserves malformed-file reporting across every existing caller.

decision: Plan issue46 execution_evidence as a checkpoint/close-scoped contract, not a handoff field
rationale: The handoff schema is explicitly immutable per PROTOCOL_RULES §P3 and additionalProperties:false, so a standardized execution_evidence must attach to the free-form checkpoint body and the session-close receipt under a new execution-evidence.schema.json validated by the CLI; this keeps a genuine executable path, narrowly extends only the validator that parses evidence (avoiding unrelated Python-validator parity), and preserves all existing workflows via all-optional inputs and a minor kernel bump 2.0.2->2.1.0 with no product/release bump.

decision: Implement issue46 evidence on checkpoint and close receipts while preserving immutable handoff and legacy omission
rationale: Resolved Opus cross-review and Hermes actual-root layout correction. Executed tests before schema/behavior/docs, retained real RED/GREEN logs, validated statuses/reasons including browser consistency, deterministic JSON and mutation rejection; 48 JS + 112 Python pass with installed-tarball roundtrip/typecheck/metadata. Package 2.1.5, kernel 2.1.0. Independent review PENDING; JOURNAL owner-deferred; no external publication or unrelated Python parser changes.

decision: Independent Opus exact-diff review of issue46 execution_evidence: CHANGES REQUESTED
rationale: At frozen HEAD 71c7b88 (base 66995ea) all executable gates are green (CLI 48/48, typecheck, test:pack tarball roundtrip, release-metadata 2.1.5; Python 112/112 + validate_state). Acceptance criteria AC1-AC4 met (optional-global + normative completion rule, two labelled examples covering all four statuses in close and checkpoint, passed/failed/not_run/blocked with required nonblank reasons and browser performed/status contradiction guard, reproducible command/CI/artifact/screenshot/branch/commit fields). AC5 only partially met: the Hermes hypothesis is CONFIRMED by temp-fixture reproduction - parseEvidenceMarkdown lacks fenced-code awareness (execution-evidence.ts:48-54, invoked at session-lifecycle.ts:369), so a checkpoint body quoting the reserved '## Execution Evidence' heading is rejected (Case A) or a nested documented example is silently parsed as real evidence (Case B), contradicting the shipped kernel's unqualified schema-free-omission compatibility claim. Fails safely (pre-mutation, no corruption). Blocking finding F1 with two small remediation options; F2 test-coverage gap; F3 trivial em-dash churn.
